en: Śrī! The Root Manual of Noble Mañjuśrī.
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in a great assembly hall for the gathering of inconceivable, marvelous, and wondrously arrayed bodhisattvas, situated in the sky above the Śuddhāvāsa heaven.
There, the Blessed One addressed the sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm:
"Listen, sons of the gods!"

I shall speak, for the benefit of all sentient beings, the mantra words that provide sustenance for all beings and fulfill their longevity, health, sovereignty, and desires—the inconceivable, marvelous, and wondrous display of the miraculous conduct, meditative concentration, purity, excellence, and liberation-circle of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Madhuśrī in his state as a youth, as well as the bodhisattva-transformations.
Listen to it; attend to it well and thoroughly, and I will speak it to you.

Then those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, with palms joined in reverence, [praised him] for his attainment of the distinguished stages, his treading upon the vajrāsana, his subduing of Māra, his turning of the wheel of Dharma, his departure from the states of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, his rebirth among gods and humans, his pacification of all suffering, his removal of poverty, disease, and affliction, his unsurpassed mastery over all mundane and supramundane mantra practices, his fulfillment of all hopes, and his unwavering retention of the words of all Tathāgatas.
"Therefore, may the Blessed One, with a mind of loving-kindness and a mind of benefit, out of compassion for us and for all sentient beings, please speak.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods with his Buddha-eye, entered the samādhi called "The Dispelling of Darkness by the Radiance of the Light of the Pure Domain."

Immediately upon the Blessed One’s entering [meditative absorption], a ray of light called "The Exhortation of the Bodhisattva Sumitabodhisattva" issued forth. Having seen the illumination of that white ray, Mañjuśrī, with a slightly smiling face, addressed that assembly of bodhisattvas:
"O sons of the Conqueror, this..."
O our mothers, let those who impel the rays be prepared here;
may you all be ready!
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, with eyes wide open and unblinking, stood facing the direction from which that radiance of light came.

Then that ray of light, having illuminated the world-system Kusumāvatī—the place of exhortation—with a great radiance, circumambulated the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, three times, and vanished into the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, rising from his seat, circumambulated the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, three times; bowing his head in prostration and placing his right knee upon the ground, he addressed the Blessed One Saṅkusumitarājendra as follows:
"The Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, has turned his attention toward me."

"O Blessed One, let us go from here to the Sahā world-system to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Blessed One Śākyamuni, in order to explain the procedures for all mantra-practices, accomplishments, and ritual maṇḍalas;

the secret rituals of the *kalpa*, the procedures for the painted cloth (*paṭa*), the heart-mantras of all Tathāgatas, the secret mudrās, and the empowerments (*abhiṣeka*), so as to fulfill all the hopes of all sentient beings.
When this was said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, spoke thus to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Go, Mañjuśrī!"
"O Prince, whatever you now deem to be the right time,
you should also inquire on our behalf whether the Blessed One Śākyamuni is free from affliction, free from illness, physically light, and dwelling in comfort."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, spoke thus to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Moreover, O Youth..."

Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as numerous as the sands of a hundred thousand Ganges rivers, have spoken, will speak, and I too now speak this: your chapter on the secret empowerment, mudrās, and ritual procedures for the maṇḍala and mantra-practice; the fulfillment of all hopes; the satisfaction of all sentient beings; the chapter on the jewel of light; the manifestation of the sovereignty and prophecy of the knowledge of the past, future, and present; the turning of mantras; the finality of the place; the time of disappearance; the chapter on the assembly; and the culmination of the practice through the traversal of all the worldly and supramundane stages of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, noble Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
This first chapter is for the purpose of rejoicing;
go, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta!
Now, at whatever time you deem appropriate,
you shall hear this Dharma discourse in the presence of Śākyamuni.
You too shall speak;
and there is a mantra for this: *namaḥ sarvatathāgatānām acintyāpratihatashāsanānām ora ra smara apratihataśāsanakumārarūpadhāriṇe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*.
This, O Youthful Mañjuśrī, is the root mantra.
It is the heart of all Tathāgatas, spoken by all Tathāgatas, and they will speak it;
you too shall now speak it,
having gone to the Sahā world-system, in detail and with full analysis, as that which accomplishes all activities.
Authorized by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, this is the supreme heart mantra; here it is: *oṃ vākya eḍa namaḥ*.
And the near-heart mantra here is: *vākya hūṃ*.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having been authorized by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarāja, entered the samādhi called "Attaining the Seat of Awakening, which is the Outflow of the Bodhisattva Practice Adorned with All Arrays.

As soon as Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had entered that samādhi, the entire world-system—extending to the four directions, the zenith, the nadir, and the intermediate points, and filling every direction—became completely filled with the Blessed Buddhas, who exclaimed:
"Excellent, excellent, O [Mañjuśrī]!"
"O Son of the Victor, as you enter into this particular samādhi,

it is impossible for all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas who have entered upon the conduct— even those established on the ten stages— to comprehend it. Then the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, having consulted together with those Blessed Buddhas, spoke this supreme heart-mantra, this most secret mantra of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, which accomplishes all aims."
The single-syllable mantra, known as the supreme secret, which brings benefit to all sentient beings, is divine and is to be accomplished by others through various specific mantra practices.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sakusumitarājendra, remained silent for a moment;
having surveyed the entire world-system with his Buddha-eye and having called to mind those Blessed Buddhas, he uttered the mantra with a mind characterized by loving-kindness.
Homage to all Buddhas!
Mañjuśrī, this mantra is the supreme heart-mantra that accomplishes all activities.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having arisen from that samādhi—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—in a mere snap of the fingers, in the space of a single blink or moment, with an intellect born of the power and strength of purity, completed the miraculous manifestation of the specific samādhi called "The Renowned" and returned to the Sahā world-system. Having arrived, he established himself in the Śuddhāvāsa realm, situated upon a great jewel-gem in the expanse of the sky above.
Having illuminated that entire abode of the Śuddhāvāsa gods with a great radiance of light rays, he entered the meditative absorption named "Illumination Adorned with Luminous Jewels."

Immediately upon his entering meditative absorption, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta miraculously manifested for the purpose of honoring the Blessed One Śākyamuni a divine rain of perfumes, garlands, ointments, wreaths, powders, and incense—a rain that established the Bodhisattvas in faultless, impartial, and sovereign wisdom. This rain fell from a celestial palace composed of many varieties of jewels, adorned with jeweled parasols, and decorated with hundreds of thousands of yojanas of divine, visible, and magnificent silk hangings; it was further embellished with divine flower banners, flags, and garlands, and draped with networks of jeweled bells that emitted sweet sounds. Having seen this wondrous, marvelous, and extraordinary miracle, this manifestation of the Bodhisattva’s supernatural power, [the assembly was moved].

Then those sons of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, their hair standing on end with joy, thinking "We must go to the Buddha," began to cry out loudly in great haste, saying: "Protect us, Blessed One!
Protect us, Śākyamuni!
Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of the Śuddhāvāsa realm.
"Do not fear, friends; do not be afraid!

This is that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who has come from the presence of the Tathāgata Sakusumitarāja in the Saṅkusumita Buddha-field in order to see, worship, and attend upon him, and to proclaim the vast, marvelous Dharma-discourse consisting of the mantra-words for the great practice of purpose."

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, having circumambulated the Blessed One Śākyamuni three times with unblinking eyes, gazed upon the Blessed One, prostrated at his feet, and addressed the Blessed One with these syllables and summary verses:
"Homage to you, the liberated one, the noble! Homage to you, the supreme among men!
Homage to you, the best of men!"
The accomplisher of the purpose of all practices;
homage to you, O lion among men, the warder-off of all misfortunes!
Salutations to you, O Great Hero!
You are the destroyer of all misfortunes.
Salutations to you, O Supreme Being!
O you of infinite merit and fragrance like the white lotus!
Homage to you, O Lotus among Men,
who purifies the mire of the three worlds!
Homage to you, the liberated one, the liberator from all suffering! Homage to you, the peaceful one, the perfect tamer of all who are untamed!
First Chapter.

Homage to you, the Siddha, who accomplishes the purpose of all mantra practices! Homage to you, the auspicious one, the most auspicious of all that is auspicious! Homage to you, the Buddha, who awakens to all phenomena!

Homage to you, the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata of all phenomena! Homage to you, the Teacher who has entered into and teaches the formless state beyond conceptual proliferation! Homage to you, the Omniscient One, who—being omniscient—is established in the establishment of the objects of knowledge, the conditioned and unconditioned, the paths of the three vehicles, and nirvāṇa.

By means of these syllables, phrases, summaries, and verses of praise, the Blessed One appeared face-to-face, having transcended world-systems in the northeastern direction, in a buddha-field named Saṅkusumita.

There, in the world-system named Kusumāvatī, dwells that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One; he teaches the Dharma—good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end—which reveals the Buddha-conduct, which is beneficial, relevant to all people, unique, complete, pure, and radiant.

He currently exists, remains, and maintains himself; he teaches the Dharma, which is a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, a state of security, the ultimate goal, and the ultimate consummation for all sentient beings.

Having been authorized by that very Blessed One, he has come here to the presence of the Blessed One at his feet. That Blessed One, the Tathāgata Saṅkusumitarājendra, inquired after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, his lightness of body, and his well-being and comfort in dwelling, and spoke thus:
"It is marvelous!..."

For it is indeed marvelous that in such a time as this, the five-fold defilement (*pañcakaṣāya*), the Buddha, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, has appeared and teaches all dharmas with words and syllables complete in every respect, delighting gods and humans with the attainment of liberation and rebirth in heaven.
How wonderful is the vigor of that Blessed One, Śākyamuni!

For indeed, while this path—which is followed by the emergence from the three realms of existence and accompanied by its own retinue—is directed toward the attainment of ultimate security in Nirvana, the Blessed One establishes even those who are unworthy therein.

Nevertheless, the minds of the Blessed Buddhas are known only by the Blessed Buddhas themselves; how could I possibly know the Buddha-transformations of the Blessed Ones, whose miraculous displays of power and sovereignty are inconceivable and marvelous? As it is said in the *Śrīmūlakalpa*: "How can I know the Buddha-transformations of the Blessed Ones?"

To know the conduct, behavior, experience, entry, and activities of this [Bodhisattva], whether by way of a brief summary or even to describe them in detail over hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons—
this which is the activity of the Tathāgatas, both collectively and individually, in their manifested forms as conditioned phenomena,
and the conduct and qualities of those who rely on ancient [teachings] to be abandoned through vision— it is the Blessed One, the Tathāgata alone, who knows this; we do not.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, seated upon a great jewel throne created by his own supernatural power and transformations, gazed intently at the Blessed One Śākyamuni. Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, with a brahmic voice—possessing the resonance of the kalaviṅka bird, the song of the cuckoo, the thunder of clouds, and the sound of a drum—which was endowed with the purpose of bringing forth the conduct of a Bodhisattva in accordance with the teaching of the Dharma preceded by former questions and directed toward those who have become Tathāgatas through various discourses.
Welcome to you, Mañjuśrī!

This is the empowerment of the secret initiation of all mantra-words, seals, and maṇḍalas, which is empowered by all Buddhas through the conduct of the Mahāsattva; it brings about the attainment of the non-regressive stage for all Bodhisattvas; it fulfills all hopes for long life, health, and sovereignty; it is the knowledge and the object of knowledge of all tantras suitable for accomplishment, including the duration of time, kingdoms, and fields; in brief, it fulfills all the hopes of all sentient beings throughout the past, future, and present; it awakens one’s own virtues and causes joy in other beings by following the practice of mantra-conduct; it effects invisibility, travel through the sky, walking on foot [through the air], the making of one wise, summoning, entry into the underworld (pātāla), malevolent rites (ābhicārika), and the attainment of all desires; it summons all Yakṣas, Yakṣiṇīs, Kiṅkaras, Piśācas, and all spirits; it restores children, the elderly, and the young to their natural state; in short, it performs all actions and fulfills all heart's desires; it is effective in malevolent, pacifying, and enriching rites. Just as it is applied and just as it is proclaimed, this Great Ritual Manual (mahākalpa) of the Jewel Chapter, the crest-jewel of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, is being spoken by us and authorized by all Buddhas for the sake of pure beings—for the benefit of many people, for the welfare of many people, and for the sake of all beings, both gods and humans. This is the treasury of Dharma.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta entered the bodhisattva samādhi called *Sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānajyotiraśmivyūhālaṅkārasañcodanī*. As soon as he had entered it, for all those beings who were suffering intensely— from the first river [of the hells] up to the world-system, and as far as the great Avīci hell— they all attained the pacification of suffering and peace.

Having exhorted all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the Blessed Buddhas, that ray of light once again vanished into the crown of the head of the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. At that moment, those Buddha-fields situated in the eastern direction were illuminated and stirred by that emission from the circle of the realm of light.

They were as follows: the Tathāgata named Jyotiṣsaumyagandhāvabhāsaśrī; the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharāja; the Tathāgata named Samantāvabhāsaśrī; the Tathāgata named Samudbhatarāja; the Tathāgata named Śālendrarāja; the Tathāgata named Lokendrarāja; the Tathāgata named Amitāyurjñānaviniścayarāja; the Tathāgata named Anantāvabhāsarājendra; and the Tathāgata named Jyotiraśmirājendra. Such Buddhas, Blessed Ones—Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones—infinite and boundless world-systems, surrounded by hosts of Bodhisattvas, gathered together in this Sahā world-system to see the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One Śākyamuni, who was dwelling in the palace of the Pure Abodes (Śuddhāvāsabhavana) and was teaching, together with Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the extensive chapter on the meaning of the mantra words for the instruction on the conduct of Bodhisattvas. Those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, assembled there.
In this same way, [it is] in the southern, western, and northern directions, as well as in the intermediate directions.

Thus, having illuminated all the Buddha-fields above, below, and across, and having put to shame all the abodes of Māra in every Buddha-field, they—surrounded by hosts of bodhisattvas and preceded by the community of śrāvakas—stood forth, desiring to display that abode of the Pure Abodes (Śuddhāvāsa), the miraculous power of the Buddhas, and the majesty of the bodhisattvas; and desiring to illuminate the unimpeded teaching of the Tathāgata, which is the extensive section on the specific samādhis for accomplishing the practice of mantras.

Namely: Subāhu, Suratna, Suvrata, Sunetra, Sūrata, Sudharma, Sarvārthasiddhi, Sarvodbhūta, Dharmodgata, Raṇogata, Raṇaśrī, Peruśrī, Acintyaśrī, Prabhākaraśrī, Prabhaśrī, Jyotiśrī, Sarvārthaśrī, Sarvaratnapāṇi, Cūḍāmaṇi, Merudhvajapāṇi, Vairocanagarbha, Ratnagarbha, Jñānagarbha, Sacintyārthagarbha, Acintyārthagarbha, Dharmodbhatagarbha, Dhvajaketu, Suketu, Anantaketu, Vimalaketu, Gaganaketu, Ratnaketu, Garjitaghoṣadundubhisvararāja, Anantāvabhāsajñānarāja, Sarvatamo’ndhakāravidhamanarāja, and Sarvavikiraṇa...

Bodhividhvaṃsanarāja, Sarvacaryātiśayajñānarāja, Lokendrarāja, Atiśayendrarāja, Vidhamanarāja, Nirdhūtarāja, Ādityarāja, Abhāvasamudgatarāja, Svabhāvasamudbhatarāja, Abhāvasvabhāvasamudgatarāja, Avivakṣitarāja, Svabhāvapuṇyābha, Lokābha, Amitābha, Mitābha, Anantābha, Sune-trābha, Susambhavābha, Arthabhāvābha, Adhṛṣya, Amṛṣya, Akarṣa, Akaniṣṭha, Amala, Anala, Dyutipati, Mati, Sukha, Mukha, Nemi, Nimi, Ketu, Ṛkṣa, Divideva, Divyanābhi, Ravana, Lokaśānti, Upāriṣṭa, Dundubhisiddha, Śiva, Ākhyadivya, Duprasaha, Durdharṣa, Durālabha, Dūraṅgama, Dūrasthita, Ūrdhvadravyatama, Khadyota, Samahadyota, Adyota, Ṛṣabha, Ābha, Sumanāya, Sumana, Mahādeva, Sunirmala, Malānta, Dānta, Sami, Sucihna, Śvetadhvaja, Imi, Kimi, Kaniṣṭha, Nikarṣa, Jīva, Sujāta, Dhūmaketu, Dhvajaketu, Śvetaketu, Suketu, Vasuketu, Vasava, Pitāmaha, Pitara, Niṣkakuru, Lokākhya, Samantākhya, Mahārūya, Śreyasi, Tejasi, Jyotikiraṇa, Samantakara, Lokaṅkara, Divaṅkara, Dīpaṅkara, Bhūtāntakara, Sarvārthaṅkara, Siddhaṅkara, Dyotiṅkara, Avabhāsaṅkara, Dundubhisvara, Rutasvara, Susvara, Anantasvara, Ketusvara, Bhūtamuni, Kanakamuni, Ṛkcchandaḥ, Kāśyapa, Cikhī, Viśvabhuk, Vipaścit, and Śākyamuni.

Then, having illuminated that palace of the Pure Abodes with these and many other Blessed Buddhas, and having taken their seats upon lotus thrones, they addressed the assembly of Bodhisattvas and the gods of the earth in this manner: Thus it was said: "O sons of noble family, there is a world-system called Sahā, belonging to this very Trichiliocosm, which is difficult to perceive, difficult to see, and difficult to encounter. There, the Tathāgata named Śākyamuni dwells, stays, and remains, teaching the Dharma to the four assemblies. That Tathāgata is one who has attained the ten powers, possesses the four fearlessnesses, is endowed with the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and is a Great Hero. He is a teacher of gods and men, a Buddha, and a Blessed One. O sons of noble family, go to that Sahā world-system to behold that Tathāgata, to pay homage to him, and to hear the Dharma from him. The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara replied to those Tathāgatas: "As you command, Blessed Ones; as you instruct, Blessed Ones. Having thus received the instructions of those Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, together with a great host of Bodhisattvas, departed from that Sahā world-system. Traveling through worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, he arrived at the Sahā world-system. Upon reaching the Sahā world-system, he approached the presence of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Arriving there, he bowed his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and circumambulated him three times to the right. Then, by means of his supernatural power, he caused the entire Sahā world-system to appear adorned with a multitude of various jewels. Having manifested such a display, he withdrew his supernatural power, sat down on a lion throne, and joined his palms toward the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. He then addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni: "Blessed One, I have come from the presence of the Tathāgatas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, to pay homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and to hear the Dharma from him. At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni emitted a light from the tuft of hair between his eyebrows, illuminating all the worlds of the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. In those worlds, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas saw the Tathāgata Śākyamuni emitting that light. Seeing it, they were filled with joy and happiness, and they all came to the presence of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Arriving there, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and circumambulated him three times to the right. They then sat down before the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and joined their palms toward the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas: "Sons of noble family, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has come from the presence of the Tathāgatas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, to pay homage to me and to hear the Dharma from me. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni: "Blessed One, we wish to see that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara. The Tathāgata Śākyamuni replied to those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas: "Sons of noble family, if you wish to see that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, you should observe the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara sitting here in the midst of this assembly, facing the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, saw the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara sitting in the midst of the assembly, facing the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Having seen him, they were filled with joy and happiness, and they all paid homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni: "Blessed One, I shall now go to the worlds of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, to pay homage to those Tathāgatas and to hear the Dharma from them. The Tathāgata Śākyamuni replied to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: "Go, son of noble family, according to your wish. You should protect yourself and guard your body, for that world-system is difficult to perceive, difficult to see, and difficult to encounter. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, having received the permission of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took leave of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and departed from the Sahā world-system. Traveling through worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, he arrived at the eastern direction. Upon reaching the eastern direction, he approached the presence of the Tathāgatas of that region. Arriving there, he bowed his head at the feet of those Tathāgatas and circumambulated them three times to the right. He then sat down before those Tathāgatas and joined his palms toward them. At that time, the Tathāgatas of the eastern direction addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: "Son of noble family, you have come from the presence of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni to pay homage to us and to hear the Dharma from us. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction addressed the Tathāgatas: "Blessed Ones, we wish to see the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. The Tathāgatas replied to those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas: "Sons of noble family, if you wish to see the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, you should observe the Tathāgata Śākyamuni sitting here in the midst of this assembly, facing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, saw the Tathāgata Śākyamuni sitting in the midst of the assembly, facing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara. Having seen him, they were filled with joy and happiness, and they all paid homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction: "Sons of noble family, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has come from the Sahā world-system to pay homage to you and to hear the Dharma from you. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni: "Blessed One, we shall now go to the Sahā world-system to pay homage to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and to hear the Dharma from him. The Tathāgata Śākyamuni replied to those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas: "Go, sons of noble family, according to your wish. You should protect yourselves and guard your bodies, for that world-system is difficult to perceive, difficult to see, and difficult to encounter. At that time, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, having received the permission of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took leave of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and departed from the eastern direction. Traveling through worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, they arrived at the Sahā world-system. Upon reaching the Sahā world-system, they approached the presence of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
