in the *Mañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, [along with] the planets, the most renowned and excellent planets marked by worldly signs.
The reality should be known from the scriptures, whether through traditional authority (*āgama*) or through realization;

it should be understood through the application of various signs (*liṅga*) by discerning the destinies and wombs [of beings], and all that is auspicious or inauspicious should be known through the cruel and the gentle signs.
Then, an umbrella, a white banner, my own flesh, and raw meat were offered; the earth was lifted up, a lotus-mechanism appeared, and cow dung was presented.
One should recognize curd, flowers, fruit, a woman adorned with garments, white cloth, and a twice-born man speaking for the sake of one's welfare as auspicious.
One should recognize a bull, an elephant, and likewise a horse adorned with chowries;
a lamp placed upon a vessel filled with grain and fruits;
or an image of a deity or a brahmin being constantly honored by kings.
Or else, for the purpose of consecration, one should [prepare] the image of the king or of the ministers.

The sound of conchs, kettledrums, tabors, and great drums; the resonant ringing of bells and the proclamation of shouts of victory; and the human voices uttered which bestow the fruit of success and victory—having announced these auspicious signs and the desired offering, one shall obtain all prosperity, security, and that which is cherished and well-honored; indeed, one shall attain every wish arising from the mind, made fruitful.

Then one who seeks accomplishment should proceed to the recitation of mantras; he should point out the attainment of success for all beings who have set out on the path. One who is the presiding deity, beloved, born of a noble lineage, and supreme—such a person should always be entreated. For one who beholds that bearer of the *liṅga*, there is fruit.
Deities are always said to possess various forms and signs; likewise, those bearers of the *liṅga* are described as having various dress and emblems.

Whoever perceives another as most beloved shall obtain the arising of the fruit for that very person. When humans on earth utter various kinds of speech, they speak auspicious words to one another, engaged in mutual conversation.
And when they speak to others, they do so with full confidence on all sides. The twenty-second chapter of the extensive [tantra] is thus declared.

And thus they spoke these auspicious and beneficial words, always reciting: "May there be security, health, prosperity, well-being, peace, and the arising of happiness for all! May the wealthy ones, the chief deities, the gods, and likewise the King of Dharma (Yama), as well as the Sun-god from every direction, protect us! And may the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, along with the *tāra* mantra, always protect us! [May there be] the auspicious, radiant golden Youth (Kumāra) and the great festival of the mass of fire!"

He heard sounds praising the Jina, Padma, Vajra, Lokeśa, and supreme enlightenment; likewise, he heard many various kinds of auspicious words, well-described by the virtuous, concerning the Bodhisattvas, the worlds, and the most excellent gods. Indeed, as he proceeded, he would attain all of these. Furthermore, he heard other sounds that were despised by the world and censured; yet for those intent on recitation, these auspicious omens are favorable for those setting out.
For all those who possess the wealth of diligence and exertion, this is my yoga; everything other than that is censured, for it does not yield the fruit of one's efforts.

One should proceed everywhere only with what is auspicious, and never with what is inauspicious. Having bowed to all the Buddhas, having performed three circumambulations, and having prostrated to one’s own mantra, the Lord of Mantras, one’s parents, and those who have undergone hardships, one should go everywhere; therein, one shall point out auspiciousness.

Having diligently honored the preceptors, the chief gurus, and the upādhyāyas, as well as the praiseworthy preachers of Dharma and those who are excellent and devoted to their vows; and having worshipped his chosen deity according to the rules, bathed, eaten, and become composed at dawn, the practitioner—having conquered his senses and being intent on purity and right conduct—should proceed toward all directions. Thus, he shall obtain auspicious results from every quarter, in accordance with the fruits of each specific direction.

In the *Mañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, peace and well-being, as well as the increase of longevity and health, and the attainment of glorious prosperity—immeasurable and exactly as desired by the mind—are proclaimed. Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the detailed section on the instruction regarding the signs of omens and the knowledge of the cries of all beings, from the *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, which is an extensive Mahāyāna sūtra belonging to the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka-avatamsaka*.
May there be auspiciousness!
